newsitem.title: USA: TV industry gets Senate deadline on ratings system.
newsitem.headline: TV industry gets Senate deadline on ratings system.

text.p: Senate lawmakers have given the television industry a week to develop a programme ratings system that satisfies parents groups or face legislation requiring changes, lawmakers said on Tuesday.
"I'm 99 percent sure that there will be an agreement," Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican told a news conference.

McCain and lawmakers from both the House and Senate met TV industry executives over efforts to revise the industry's age-based ratings. Industry officials are negotiating with parents groups over adding the labels "S" for sexual content, "V" for violence and "L" for adult language to existing ratings that took effect on Jan. 1.
Representative Edward Markey, a Massachusetts Democrat, said industry officials are reluctant to add content warnings to certain children's shows.
"The message to broadcasters is, time is up. You must no longer delay in giving parents the warnings they want on TV shows," Markey told the news conference.
Two bills are working their way through the Senate. One, sponsored by Sen. Ernest Hollings, a South Carolina Democrat, would force the industry to label violent shows or air them only after 10 p.m.
A second, sponsored by Sen. Dan Coates, an Indiana Republican, would make a content-based ratings system a condition for broadcasters having their licenses renewed.
McCain said lawmakers would suspend efforts in passing the legislation if the industry and parents groups can agree on a ratings system.
